catalogue.final:
Re-running wrote nothing: the latest transaction is still the authority write, so the load is idempotent.

## Catalogue report (2026-10-03)

**Indexed**

| Source | Records |
|---|---|
| Shopify products | 49 variants |
| Shopify orders | 26,546 orders, 37,773 lines, 21,129 customer accounts |
| Amazon orders | 38,264 orders, 43,513 lines |
| Amazon listings | 25 listings, 25 ASINs, 25 FNSKUs |
| Amazon FBA inbound | 49 shipments |
| 3PL | 49 item codes, 29 receipts, 146 receipt lines, 37,331 outbound lines |
| QuickBooks vendor list | 11 vendors, 8 of them factories |

These counts equal the distinct IDs in each source.

**Crosswalk**
- **Hubs:** there are 49, one per SKU, and every hub carries all of these: Shopify variant, UPC, 3PL item code, factory item code, HS code and supplier.
- **Shopify:** 34 hubs match exactly (confidence 1). 15 have a broken spelling in Shopify and are matched at 0.9. The broken spellings include `AH-CTB-16-LRG`, `AHUTN0017NAT` and lowercase `ah-btl-0020-blk`. Each hub uses the canonical `AH-XXX-NNNN-CCC` spelling.
- **3PL:** all 49 matched on UPC (1.0). 15 of the 3PL's Client SKUs are blank or mistyped, for example `BKL`, `HFL` and `BMA`. I left those in the source.
- **Amazon:** all 25 listings point at a hub. 11 match exactly. 14 carry an `-FBA` suffix or a different spelling and are matched at 0.9. No two listings share an ASIN.
- **Factory codes and HS codes:** all 49 factory items matched a hub by exact description (0.7). They were read from the commercial invoices and are written as `NBBW:MT-1574`.
- **Suppliers:** 8 supplier codes are linked to their QuickBooks vendor (0.9) by legal name. Three vendors have no supplier code (forwarder, customs broker and the 3PL) and are indexed under the vendor name alone.

**Attributes registered:** none. The installed vocabulary already covered everything.

**Duplicate accounts:** 154 `core/same_as`, each pointing at the oldest account.
- 85 at 0.9 (same mailbox after dropping a `+alias`).
- 69 at 0.7 (same full name and postal address, often at a different mail domain).
- None at 1 (no two accounts share an identical mailbox).
- I read ten pairs from each rule and found no pair of different people. No account has more than two others pointing at it.

**Checks**
- **Bare records:** the 26 bare PO records are expected, since the receipts name them and ingestion fills them. No SKU, listing or item record is bare.
- **Sources left out:**
  - `quickbooks/transaction_list_by_vendor.csv` is general ledger, which is never indexed.
  - The WeChat chats and ops inbox are documents for the ingestion skill.
  - The PO, PI, inspection (LCI) and commercial invoice PDFs are also left to ingestion. I read only the PI and invoice PDFs, for the item and HS codes.
  - The 3PL inventory snapshot is not indexed as records. It only supplied the item codes.
- **Re-run:** it wrote nothing.

**Terms the sources disagree on**
- **SKU:**
  - Shopify and the 3PL (Client SKU) have typos and drift from our code.
  - Amazon appends `-FBA` to some seller SKUs.
  - I kept Amazon's spelling on `amazon/seller_sku`.
- **On hand:** Shopify's `inventoryQuantity` equals the 3PL's Available, not its On Hand. For example kettle BLK shows 3,223 in Shopify against 3,235 on hand at the 3PL. These are values, so they stay in the source.

**For a human to decide**
- 33 receipt rows have a blank PO reference, so I wrote no `receipt/po` for those lines. Receipts 000007, 000008 and 000013 are examples.
- The FBA inbound export has shipment totals only, so I could not write `amazon/fba_line`. Four FBA shipments have no outbound lines in the 3PL file.
- Name-and-address matches across mail domains (such as `evelynrobinson2@` at `.com` and `.org`) are a judgement call. The 69 at 0.7 can be reviewed or retracted.

The load script is `work/load.py`, with helpers `fac.py` and `cust.py`.

ingest.final:
I ingested all 1,109 documents into the fact store, and every write cites its source document. A dry run raised no errors, the real run wrote 422 transactions, and the store counts match what I parsed.

## Documents read
| Kind | Count |
|---|---|
| Proforma invoices | 48 |
| Commercial invoice and packing lists | 41 |
| Inspection reports | 46 (42 passed, 4 failed) |
| Chat messages | 811, from 8 supplier chats |
| Emails | 163 (104 forwarder, 30 broker, 29 warehouse) |

- **Documents created:** 407 (the 24 already in the store are separate from these). Only documents that gave facts got a store entity.
- **Skipped as already read:** none. The catalogue had cited 15 of the commercial invoices, but only for item codes, supplier links and HS codes, so I read them in full.
- **Issue dates corrected:** those 15 documents carried the catalogue's write time as their issue date. They now carry the invoice date.
- **Chat time zone:** I read the chat timestamps as New York time, as you said.

## What the store now holds
- **Purchase orders:** 48, with 196 lines, supplier details and a status. 37 are received, 4 shipped, 5 in production, 1 ready and 1 confirmed.
- **Shipments:** 32 (31 with a house bill, plus one booked only), with 166 shipment lines and 29 deliveries.
- **Inspections and customs:** 46 inspections and 30 customs entries.
- **Shared containers:** each shipment that several POs share is one entity. For example, the bill PBLHB2500004 carries three POs.
- **HS codes:** no HS code on an invoice differed from the one on the SKU, so nothing needed reporting.

## Facts below confidence 1
- **PO ETD slips (0.8):** 18 of these. The supplier gave a date with no year, and some named the order by their own PI number rather than our PO number. I took each as the next occurrence of that date, in China time, after the message.
- **`in_production` status from a deposit acknowledgement (0.9 or 0.8):** 43 of these. The acknowledgement doesn't name the PO, so I linked it to the preceding deposit message. That link is 0.9 when the deposit names the PO and 0.8 when I matched it by the deposit amount (the PI total times the deposit percentage).
- **Container numbers from chat (0.9):** 15 of these. The "loaded today" messages name no PO. I matched each to a shipment through the supplier's POs, then checked the container against the later invoice.

## Unresolved and gaps
- **PO "sent" status:** I didn't record it. The skill's status table doesn't say when to set it, so POs sent but without a PI have no status.
- **Warehouse discrepancies:** the store has no attribute for counts received or damaged. 21 of the 29 receipts list discrepancies. For example, one receipt shows ACMH-10294 as 576 expected and 552 received.
- **Other chat content with no attribute:**
  - price changes: +3% from 1 March, +4% from 1 May, −2% from 1 July and +5% from 15 August;
  - the deposit and balance payments, and the DHL sample couriers;
  - holiday closures (Chinese New Year and National Day).
- **Not recorded, in a document only:** customs broker invoices, last-free-day dates, cut-offs, and bank details on the PIs.
- **Ambiguous production messages:** six "大货生产中" messages were left out. Each supplier's POs were already in production, so they added nothing.
- **Open items at the end of the data:** one booking (PBLXMN2609032, for PO-2026-0023) has no pre-alert yet, and PO-2026-0019 to 0022 are shipped but not yet delivered.

rerun.final:
This is a re-run on unchanged sources, so I wrote nothing to the store. The step 7 checks found no errors, but I read only 35 of the 154 duplicate pairs against the source.

## Sources and counts
Every source count matches the store.

| Source | Distinct IDs in source | In store |
|---|---|---|
| Shopify orders | 26,546 | 26,546 |
| Shopify customers | 21,129 | 21,129 |
| Shopify line items | 37,773 | 37,773 |
| Shopify products and variants | 49 variants | 49 hubs |
| Amazon orders | 38,264 | 38,264 |
| Amazon order lines | 43,513 | 43,513 |
| Amazon listings | 25 | 25 |
| FBA inbound shipments | 49 | 49 |
| 3PL outbound lines | 37,331 | 37,331 |
| 3PL receipts | 29 (146 lines) | 29 (146 lines) |
| 3PL items | 49 | 49 |
| QuickBooks vendors | 11 | 11 |

- **Left out:** `quickbooks/transaction_list_by_vendor.csv`, because it is general-ledger bills and never indexed.
- **Left to ingestion:** `supplier_docs`, `wechat` and `email`, because they hold documents and messages. The store already holds 431 documents and the POs, shipments, QC reports and customs entries read from them.
- **Not indexed:** `amazon/fba_inventory.txt` and `3pl/inventory_snapshot.csv`. Their rows name only seller SKUs and item codes that are already on the store's hubs and listings.
- **Crosswalk and field authority:** both unchanged.

## Checks
- **Join-key records created by mistake:** none.
  - Amazon order IDs and Shopify customer IDs are all well-formed.
  - Ten 3PL receipts (`GSF-RCV-000007`, `08`, `13`, `15`, `18`, `19`, `20`, `25`, `27`, `29`) hold nothing but their number. Their `Reference` is blank in the source, so no PO ref can be written. These are expected.
  - Three QuickBooks vendors are bare: Pacific Bridge Logistics, Harborline Customs Brokerage and Garden State Fulfillment. They are not suppliers, so they have no supplier record.
- **Duplicates:** the store has 154 `core/same_as` links.
  - I checked a sample of 35 against the source names, mailboxes and addresses.
  - 20 share a normalized mailbox.
  - 13 share the same mailbox name at different providers, such as `thomas.brian@mail.example` and `thomas.brian@example.org`. All 13 also share the same name and shipping address, so I judge them sound.
  - 2 share name and address only.
  - No account has more than three others pointing at it. One account, `9086421013740`, has two pointing at it.
  - I didn't check the other 119 pairs.
- **Sources left out:** accounted for above.
- **Counts:** all match.

## Terms the sources disagree on
I found nothing new.

## For a person to decide
- **Different-provider mailbox rule:** it is outside the skill's stated rules. It looks right on the sample, but you should confirm you want it kept.
- **Blank-reference receipts:** the 10 receipts above need a PO from the warehouse or the supplier documents.
